title: “A demand for agency” | Culture Action Europe’s State of Culture 2026 is out
content:
“If this report amounts to one finding above all the others, it is this: recognition was never the finish line, only the starting condition. Culture’s value has rarely been stated this clearly or this often by European institutions and, yet, it still has not been matched by the funding, protection, or governance necessary for it to be realised. Two years ago, the question this report asked was whether culture could be heard at all. This edition asks a harder one: now that it has been, what is it actually allowed to do with that recognition?”
— Lars Ebert, State of Culture 2026

The central contradiction running through State of Culture 2026 is that culture is praised more than ever and protected less than ever. It is a public good in every EU institution’s vocabulary, yet still funded and evaluated as though it were an industrial output, measured in projects, KPIs and short cycles.
